Freelance:Shot.definition: Definition: Team-relative selection weight for ending a meaningful offensive involvement with a shot attempt. Higher values increase scoring aggression after opportunity exists. In live gameplay, higher Shot does not guarantee higher FGA when another player has materially greater Touch, initiation, play-type, or reset involvement. Use possession-ending evidence for the historical baseline, then normalize Shot and Touch together across the current roster. Validate full simulation separately.

Freelance:Touches.definition: Definition: Team-relative live-game opportunity and involvement weight. It affects how often the offense seeks, initiates through, returns to, or keeps the player involved through catches, handling, passes, handoffs, post entries, screens, resets, and playmaking decisions. Moderate Touch gaps can create large differences in meaningful opportunities and total attempts. Touch is not a direct conversion of raw NBA touches and must be normalized across the entire roster. It does not require the player to shoot.

Jump Shooting:Shot Close.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for attempting shots from the short close-range area, generally outside the immediate under-basket zone but inside the mid-range area. This can include short push shots, hooks, runners, short fades, and other close attempts. It controls the location preference, while specific tendencies such as Floater or post moves help select the shot type.

Jump Shooting:Shot Under Basket.definition: Definition: Selection weight for immediately attempting a point-blank shot once the player is already under or directly beside the basket. This includes standing layups, dump-off finishes, seals, dunker-spot catches, and quick no-dribble attempts. It does not create the positioning or control Driving Layup, Driving Dunk, offensive rebounding, or Putback frequency.

Jump Shooting:Shot Mid-Range.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from the mid-range area. This acts as the global mid-range volume gate, while Spot-Up Mid, Off-Screen Mid, Dribble Pull-Up Mid, Stepback Mid, post shots, and other contextual tendencies help determine how those mid-range attempts are created.

Jump Shooting:Spot Up Shot Mid-Range.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for taking a mid-range jumper from a stationary or settled catch. This includes elbow catches, face-up catches, pick-and-pop opportunities, short-roll catches, and traditional catch-and-shoot mids. It does not control total mid-range volume and should operate beneath the player’s Shot Mid tendency. Because this is a rare modern shot type, values above 35 should be reserved for documented specialists.

Jump Shooting:Off Screen Shot Mid-Range.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for taking a mid-range jumper after off-ball movement or a screening action, including curls, pindowns, flares, handoffs, relocations, and movement catches. It does not control total mid-range volume and should operate beneath Shot Mid and alongside play types and playbook actions. Modern offenses usually convert these actions into threes or drives, so values above 30 require clear film evidence.

Jump Shooting:Shot Three.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from three-point range. This acts as the global three-point volume gate, while Spot-Up Three, Off-Screen Three, Dribble Pull-Up Three, Stepback Jumper Three, Transition Pull-Up Three, Contested Jumper Three, play types, and team spacing help determine how those attempts are created. This does not determine three-point accuracy.

Jump Shooting:Spot Up Shot Three.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for taking a three-point jumper from a stationary or settled catch when a viable perimeter shot is available. This includes traditional spot-ups, kickouts, drive-and-kick catches, pick-and-pop catches, trail opportunities, and settled relocation catches. It does not control total three-point volume and should operate beneath the player’s Shot Three tendency.

Jump Shooting:Off Screen Shot Three.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for taking a three-point jumper after off-ball movement or a screening action, including curls, pindowns, flares, handoffs, relocations, screen-assisted catches, and movement into pop or spacing opportunities. It does not control total three-point volume and should operate beneath Shot Three alongside play types and playbook actions.

Jump Shooting:Contested Jumper Mid-Range.definition: Definition: Selection weight for attempting a mid-range jumper when the defender remains close, attached, recovering, or actively contesting. Higher values increase willingness to shoot through pressure after a mid-range opportunity exists. This does not control overall mid-range volume, shooting ability, or contest success.

Jump Shooting:Contested Jumper Three.definition: Definition: Selection weight for attempting a three-point jumper when the defender is close, recovering, attached, or actively contesting. Higher values increase willingness to shoot through perimeter pressure after a three-point opportunity exists. This does not control overall three-point volume, shooting ability, or contest success.

Jump Shooting:Stepback Jumper Mid-Range.definition: Definition: Selection weight for converting a stepback, retreat dribble, or backward escape into a mid-range jumper. This is the shot-selection tendency after separation is created and is separate from Driving Step Back, normal pull-up mids, spot-up mids, post fades, and off-screen mid-range shots.

Jump Shooting:Stepback Jumper Three.definition: Definition: Selection weight for converting a stepback, retreat dribble, pull-back escape, or backward separation move into a three-point jumper. This is separate from Driving Step Back, normal pull-up threes, spot-up threes, off-screen threes, and general three-point volume.

Jump Shooting:Spin Jumper.definition: Definition: Selection weight for attempting a jumper after using a spin or turn-around dribble move to create separation. This is for self-created spinning jump shots, not post spins, post fades, regular pull-ups, stepbacks, or driving spin finishes.

Jump Shooting:Transition Pull Up Three.definition: Definition: Selection weight for taking a self-created pull-up three while advancing the ball in transition or early offense before the defense and half-court action are fully established. This excludes catch-and-shoot transition threes, trail threes, ordinary half-court pull-ups, and stepback threes.

Jump Shooting:Drive Pull Up Mid-Range.definition: Definition: Selection weight for taking a mid-range jumper off the live dribble after creating space with movement, pace, a screen, or a stop-and-rise action. This identifies the pull-up shot form and is separate from overall mid-range volume, spot-up mids, off-screen mids, stepbacks, floaters, post fades, and contested-shot willingness.

Jump Shooting:Drive Pull Up Three.definition: Definition: Selection weight for taking a three-point jumper off the live dribble after creating space with movement, pace, a screen, hesitation, or stop-and-rise action. This identifies the pull-up shot form and is separate from overall three-point volume, spot-up threes, off-screen threes, transition pull-up threes, stepback threes, and contested-shot willingness.

Driving:Drive.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for initiating an on-ball drive from the perimeter, face-up position, or live-dribble action. Higher values make the player more likely to put the ball on the floor and attack rather than remain in a shooting, passing, or reset branch. This does not control drive success, drive commitment after an advantage is created, finishing type, or contact seeking.

Driving:Spot Up Drive.definition: Definition: Willingness to attack off the catch from a stationary or spaced position when the defender closes out, rotates late, or gives a driving lane. This is for catch-and-go attacks, not isolation drives, pick-and-roll ball handling, off-screen attacks, or self-created dribble breakdowns.

Driving:Off Screen Drive.definition: Definition: Conditional willingness to attack after receiving the ball from an off-ball screen or movement action, including curls, pindowns, handoffs, and similar catches. This is a movement-drive branch, not a general Drive rating and not a label for rim runners who do not handle the ball in these actions.

Jump Shooting:Use Glass.definition: Definition: Selection weight for using the backboard on an eligible layup or close finish when the approach angle allows it. Higher values favor a bank finish over a direct finish. This does not increase layup frequency, determine finishing ability, or apply to ordinary bank jump shots.

Jump Shooting:Step Through Shot.definition: Definition: Selection weight for using step-through footwork after a defender commits, allowing the player to move around or underneath the contest before attempting a close shot or layup. This can occur from a drive, paint catch, face-up, or post-adjacent situation and is separate from post-move tendencies.

Layups And Dunks:Driving Layup.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of attempting a standard layup while attacking the rim with forward momentum when a viable layup window exists. Higher values make driving layups a larger part of the player’s finishing package. This does not control drive initiation, layup ability or success, contact frequency, Driving Dunk, Floater, or special gather selection.

Layups And Dunks:Spin Layup.definition: Definition: Selection weight for using a spin gather or spinning layup finish after entering the paint. The spin is part of the finishing sequence and may change the player’s angle around the defender. This is separate from Driving Spin, post spins, and ordinary reverse layups.

Layups And Dunks:Euro Step Layup.definition: Definition: Selection weight for using a two-step lateral gather to avoid or move around a defender before a layup or dunk attempt. This does not increase drive frequency, create the finishing window, or guarantee that the Eurostep succeeds.

Layups And Dunks:Hop Step Layup.definition: Definition: Selection weight for using a hop gather or jump-stop-style finishing move to change the approach angle, create space, split defenders, or absorb contact before a layup or dunk. This is a finishing gather and is separate from hop jumpers or stationary shot footwork.

Layups And Dunks:Floater.definition: Definition: Selection weight for attempting a soft runner, push shot, or floater from the lane before reaching the immediate rim area, usually to score over or around interior defenders. This is separate from ordinary close shots, pull-up mid-range jumpers, and standard driving layups.

Layups And Dunks:Standing Dunk.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of attempting a dunk from a stationary or near-stationary position at the rim after a catch, seal, offensive rebound, drop-step, or completed stop. Higher values favor a standing dunk over a standing layup when the player is eligible. This does not control standing-dunk ability, success, positioning, or how often the player reaches the rim.

Layups And Dunks:Driving Dunk.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of attempting a dunk while attacking the rim with forward momentum. Higher values favor a driving dunk over a driving layup when a viable dunk window exists. This does not control drive frequency, dunk ability, success, contact-dunk eligibility, or flashy-dunk style.

Layups And Dunks:Flashy Dunk.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of choosing a flashy, acrobatic, forceful, or higher-risk dunk animation instead of a safer basic dunk after a dunk attempt has already been selected. This does not increase overall dunk frequency, create a dunk window, or determine dunk success.

Layups And Dunks:Alley-Oop.definition: Definition: Frequency of attempting to receive and finish lob passes when a viable opportunity is available. Higher values make the player a more active vertical target and more willing to complete alley-oop finishes. This does not control how often the player throws lob passes.

Layups And Dunks:Putback.definition: Definition: Frequency of immediate scoring attempts after securing or touching an offensive rebound. Higher values favor tips, lay-ins, dunks, or quick go-back-up attempts instead of securing the ball and resetting. This does not control how often the player crashes the offensive glass or obtains the rebound.

Layups And Dunks:Crash.definition: Definition: Conditional frequency that meaningful contact during an attacking finish produces a stumble, loss of balance, crash, or fall-to-the-floor outcome. Crash does not create the drive, contact opportunity, foul call, or finishing attempt itself. It is separate from Drive, Attack Strong on Drive, Draw Foul/FTA, size/strength/physicality, offensive rebounding, and Putback.

Driving:Drive Right.definition: Definition: Drive Right is directional preference after a drive opportunity exists; Drive controls how often the player drives. Below 50 favors left, above 50 favors right, and 50 means genuinely balanced direction, never unknown or missing research. Use player-specific evidence in this order: left-versus-right event/tracking data → multi-game film or manual charting → explicit directional scouting. Dominant hand is supporting context only. NBA.com Drives establishes volume, not direction. Drive 30+ players with unresolved direction must not be finalized at 50; very low-volume drivers may use 50 only as documented low-opportunity neutral.

Drive Setup:Triple Threat Pump Fake.definition: Definition: Conditional frequency of selecting a shot fake from a stationary or triple-threat catch before shooting, driving, passing, or resetting. For interior players, this includes standing up-fakes near the basket. Higher values increase branch selection, not effectiveness. Keep the value evidence-based because excessive settings can create unnecessary pump-fake spam even when defender pressure does not warrant it.

Drive Setup:Triple Threat Jab Step.definition: Definition: Conditional frequency of selecting a jab-step probe from triple-threat stance before shooting, driving, passing, or resetting. Higher values increase jab selection, not creation ability. Use repeated real behavior rather than handle ratings or generic creator status, because excessive settings can produce repeated or unnecessary jabs.

Drive Setup:Triple Threat Idle.definition: Definition: Conditional tendency to remain in the neutral stationary triple-threat state when an immediate shoot, jab, pump fake, drive, pass, or other active action does not take priority. Higher values increase willingness to stay neutral before another action is selected. This does not represent basketball IQ, general patience, total time of possession, or overall decision speed. Do not automatically lower Idle for limited creators or traditional bigs just to make them act quicker; moderate or high Idle can correctly discourage manufactured offense when no immediate action is available. Quick rim finishing is governed separately by scoring/finishing tendencies and context. A high-Idle player can still immediately shoot, pass, drive, or initiate when another action wins first.

Drive Setup:Triple Threat Shoot.definition: Definition: Conditional frequency of immediately converting a stationary or triple-threat catch into a scoring attempt before holding or beginning a dribble sequence. Depending on location, this can be a jumper, standing interior shot, or quick catch-and-finish. It is not the universal control for immediate interior finishing: Shot Under Basket, Shot Close, Standing Dunk, Driving Dunk, Putback and other contextual finishing logic can independently produce an immediate attempt even when Triple Threat Shoot is low.

tiers.label: Holds or Initiates Instead of Scoring

Drive Setup:Setup With Sizeup.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a stationary or near-stationary size-up dribble used before the player commits to a drive, shot, or pass. This competes with No Setup Dribble when the pre-attack setup branch is available and is separate from the live-drive move tendencies.

tiers.label: Regular Size-Up Usage / NBA Norm Ceiling

Drive Setup:Setup With Hesitation.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a hesitation-style setup used before the player commits to a drive, shot, or pass. This competes with No Setup Dribble when the pre-attack setup branch is available and is separate from Driving Dribble Hesitation after the drive begins.

tiers.label: Regular Setup Hesitation / NBA Norm Ceiling

Drive Setup:No Setup Dribble.definition: Definition: Selection weight for skipping pre-attack setup dribbles and moving directly into a drive, shot, pass, or play action. Lower values open the setup branch more often; higher values favor quicker initiation. This is independent from No Drive Dribble Move, which applies only after the player has begun attacking.

Driving:Driving Crossover.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a crossover used as a live-drive change-of-direction counter after the player begins attacking. This competes with No Drive Dribble Move, so a high value identifies a preferred move without requiring it on every drive.

Driving:Driving Double Crossover.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a chained two-direction crossover used during a live drive. This is a specialized combo counter, not two ordinary crossovers performed separately.

Driving:Driving Spin.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a full spin used to change direction or protect the ball during a live drive. The move can lead to a continued attack, pass, pull-up, or finish and is separate from Spin Layup.

Driving:Driving Half Spin.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a half-spin feint or partial turn used to change the drive angle, freeze the defender, or reset the attack without completing a full spin. Assign independently from Driving Spin.

Driving:Driving Step Back.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a retreat or step-back dribble used during a live drive to create space, reset the angle, or reattack. It does not automatically produce a jumper and is separate from Stepback Jumper tendencies.

Driving:Driving Behind The Back.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a behind-the-back dribble used during a live drive to protect the ball, change direction, or avoid a defender. This is separate from stationary setup or size-up dribbling.

Driving:Driving Dribble Hesitation.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of a hesitation used after the drive begins to pause the defender, change pace, or explode into a second burst. This is separate from Setup Hesitation before the attack.

Driving:Driving In And Out.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight of an in-and-out dribble used during a live drive to fake a change of direction while keeping the ball on the same side and continuing the attack. This is deception, not a crossover.

Driving:No Driving Dribble Move.definition: Definition: Selection weight for a simple or straight-line continuation instead of a driving dribble move once the player is attacking. Lower values open the move branch more often; higher values favor direct drives. This competes with the individual driving-move tendencies rather than completely disabling them.

tiers.label: Almost Always Uses a Move or Counter

Driving:Attack Strong On Drive.definition: Definition: Controls willingness to continue the downhill attack toward the basket once a drive has begun or a driving advantage is created. Higher values make the player turn the corner, continue penetration and pressure the paint instead of stopping short for an early pull-up or reset. Lower values increase early pull-ups, perimeter stops, resets, or abandoned penetration. Drive controls how often the attack begins. Drive Step Back is a separate retreat/counter choice that can stop or reset the attack when help arrives. Crash is a separate contact-fall outcome after a finish meets contact.

Passing:Dish To Open Man.definition: Definition: Conditional preference for passing to an open teammate after the player creates an advantage, draws help, penetrates the defense, or reaches a finishing decision. Higher values favor kickouts, dump-offs, and open-man passes over keeping the ball or forcing a shot. This is not general passing frequency, passing accuracy, or overall playmaking ability, and excessive values may cause early bailouts before the defense is fully pressured.

Passing:Flashy Pass.definition: Definition: Secondary pass-style selection tendency that controls how often the player chooses a creative, deceptive, stylish, or higher-risk pass animation after a pass has already been selected. This can include no-look, behind-the-back, wraparound, improvised, and other expressive passes. It does not increase general passing frequency or determine passing accuracy.

Passing:Alley-Oop Pass.definition: Definition: Frequency of attempting alley-oop passes when a teammate is cutting, rolling, slipping, or running toward the rim and the game detects a viable lob window. Higher values increase willingness to choose the lob instead of a normal pass and may cause the player to accept more marginal lob windows. This does not create the opening, determine pass accuracy, or control the receiver’s finish.

Freelance:Roll vs. Pop.definition: Definition: Directional preference after the player actually sets a screen. Higher values favor rolling, diving, or slipping toward the basket. Lower values favor popping, fading, or spacing away from the screen. This does not determine screen frequency, screen quality, or whether the player is used as a screener.

Freelance:Spot vs. Cut.definition: Definition: General off-ball positioning preference when the player is not handling the ball or completing a screen action. Higher values favor remaining spaced, relocating around the perimeter, or settling into spot-up positions. Lower values favor cutting, diving, filling open interior space, or moving toward the basket. This does not determine how often plays call for cuts or spot-ups.

Freelance:Iso vs. Elite Defender.definition: Definition: Conditional willingness to attack one-on-one when the player’s primary defender is an elite defensive matchup. Higher values increase the likelihood that the player attacks individually rather than continuing the current team action. This does not determine isolation ability, scoring success, or total offensive usage; Play Discipline, Touch, play types, and team role still govern whether the opportunity occurs.

Freelance:Iso vs. Good Defender.definition: Definition: Conditional willingness to attack one-on-one when the player’s primary defender is a good or above-average defensive matchup. Higher values increase the likelihood that the player attacks individually rather than continuing the current team action. This does not determine isolation ability, scoring success, or total offensive usage; Play Discipline, Touch, play types, and team role still govern whether the opportunity occurs.

Freelance:Iso vs. Average Defender.definition: Definition: Conditional willingness to attack one-on-one when the player’s primary defender is an average defensive matchup. Higher values increase the likelihood that the player attacks individually rather than continuing the current team action. This does not determine isolation ability, scoring success, or total offensive usage; Play Discipline, Touch, play types, and team role still govern whether the opportunity occurs.

Freelance:Iso vs. Poor Defender.definition: Definition: Conditional willingness to attack one-on-one when the player’s primary defender is a poor or exploitable defensive matchup. Higher values increase the likelihood that the player attacks individually rather than continuing the current team action. This does not determine isolation ability, scoring success, or total offensive usage; Play Discipline, Touch, play types, and team role still govern whether the opportunity occurs.

tiers.label: Avoids Isolation Even vs Poor Defenders

Freelance:Play Discipline.definition: Definition: Controls how strictly and how long the player follows a called play, assigned action, or team structure before freelancing into a shot, drive, isolation, reset, or improvised decision. Higher values increase adherence to the designed action. Lower values give the player greater freedom to abandon the action early. This is not basketball IQ, decision quality, coachability, or general unselfishness.

Post Game:Post Up.definition: Definition: Frequency and selection weight for establishing, requesting, or accepting a post possession. This is the post-opportunity gate, not the shot decision. Assign primarily from post-up possessions, post touches, role, multi-year usage, and film; size, strength, or interior scoring ability alone do not justify a high value.

Post Game:Post Back Down.definition: Definition: Conditional preference for controlled backing down after a post catch. This represents patient pressure and measured displacement, not general post-up frequency. Assign from actual backdown behavior and keep separate from Post Aggressive Back Down.

Post Game:Post Aggressive Backdown.definition: Definition: Conditional preference for forceful, displacement-oriented bumps after a post catch. This is not a general strength or post-scoring rating. It should normally remain 10-20 points below Post Back Down unless repeated bully-style possessions are clearly supported by film.

Post Game:Post Face Up.definition: Definition: Conditional preference to turn and face the defender from a post catch before shooting, driving, passing, or countering. This can be high for mobile bigs and wings even when Back Down is moderate.

Post Game:Post Spin.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for a spin counter after post control is established. Assign from move-specific usage and film, not from general post skill or versatility.

Post Game:Post Drive.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for driving toward the rim from a face-up or post-controlled catch. This is separate from the global Drive tendency and requires post or face-up opportunity.

Post Game:Post Drop Step.definition: Definition: Conditional selection weight for using a drop step from established post position. Assign from actual move usage and interior role, not standing-dunk ability, strength, or size alone.

Post Game:Shoot From Post.definition: Definition: Conditional likelihood of ending an established post possession with a shot instead of passing, holding, resetting, or exiting. High Post Up does not require equally high Shoot From Post; passing hubs should often separate them.

Post Game:Post Hook Left.definition: Definition: Conditional hook selection toward the left after a hook opportunity exists. This is a move-direction branch, not a general post-scoring rating. Assign from actual hook attempts and shoulder/turn preference, not handedness alone.

Post Game:Post Hook Right.definition: Definition: Conditional hook selection toward the right after a hook opportunity exists. This is a move-direction branch, not a general post-scoring rating. Assign from actual hook attempts and shoulder/turn preference, not handedness alone.

Post Game:Post Fade Left.definition: Definition: Conditional fadeaway selection toward the left after a fade opportunity exists. Assign from actual directional fade usage, not general mid-range ability or post reputation.

Post Game:Post Fade Right.definition: Definition: Conditional fadeaway selection toward the right after a fade opportunity exists. Assign from actual directional fade usage, not general mid-range ability or post reputation.

Post Game:Post Shimmy Shot.definition: Definition: Conditional shoulder fake or body feint from established post position before a shot or counter. This is a rare move-specific branch and should require recurring film evidence.

Post Game:Post Hop Shot.definition: Definition: Conditional post-specific lateral or backward hop used to create separation before a jumper. This is separate from Hop Step Layup and should be reserved for documented specialists.

Post Game:Post Step Back Shot.definition: Definition: Conditional retreat or separation jumper from post control. This is separate from perimeter stepback tendencies and should be assigned from move-specific post film.

Post Game:Post Up And Under.definition: Definition: Conditional post shot-fake counter followed by a step-around, step-through, or under finish. This is separate from Triple Threat Pump Fake and general Step Through Shot and should be reserved for documented usage.

Defense:Take Charge.definition: Definition: Willingness to establish legal position and attempt to draw an offensive foul. Higher values increase charge attempts; excessive values can make defenders plant unnecessarily instead of contesting normally.

Defense:Foul.definition: Definition: Overall likelihood that a player's defensive actions end in a foul, including reaches, contests, blocks, rotations, and physical contact. This controls foul risk, not the severity of the foul.

Defense:Hard Foul.definition: Definition: Conditional willingness to use an unusually forceful, deliberate, or severe foul/stop once a foul or defensive-stop opportunity exists. Higher values favor hard wrap-ups, forceful collisions, deliberate hard transition/rim stops, or comparable severe contact rather than ordinary fouls. This does not control total foul frequency and must not be assigned from general physicality, strength, aggressive defense, blocks, contests, steals, or defensive reputation.

Defense:Pass Interception.definition: Definition: Willingness to anticipate, jump, or reach into passing lanes. Higher values create more interception attempts and gambles; they do not represent interception skill or success by themselves.

Defense:On-Ball Steal.definition: Definition: Willingness to reach, swipe, or directly attack the ball while guarding the ball handler. Higher values create more steal attempts, whiffs, and possible fouls; they do not represent steal ability by themselves.

Defense:Block Shot.definition: Definition: Willingness to leave the floor or attempt a swat when challenging a shot. Higher values create more block attempts and possible defensive mistakes; attributes, positioning, and sliders determine success.

Defense:Contest Shot.definition: Definition: Willingness to challenge shots with a closeout, hand-up contest, body challenge, or vertical contest. Higher values create more contest attempts and effort; they do not represent contest quality or shot-deterrence ability by themselves.

Jump Shooting:Shot Mid Left.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from the mid-range area. This acts as the global mid-range volume gate, while Spot-Up Mid, Off-Screen Mid, Dribble Pull-Up Mid, Stepback Mid, post shots, and other contextual tendencies help determine how those mid-range attempts are created.

Jump Shooting:Shot Mid Left-Center.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from the mid-range area. This acts as the global mid-range volume gate, while Spot-Up Mid, Off-Screen Mid, Dribble Pull-Up Mid, Stepback Mid, post shots, and other contextual tendencies help determine how those mid-range attempts are created.

Jump Shooting:Shot Mid Center.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from the mid-range area. This acts as the global mid-range volume gate, while Spot-Up Mid, Off-Screen Mid, Dribble Pull-Up Mid, Stepback Mid, post shots, and other contextual tendencies help determine how those mid-range attempts are created.

Jump Shooting:Shot Mid Right-Center.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from the mid-range area. This acts as the global mid-range volume gate, while Spot-Up Mid, Off-Screen Mid, Dribble Pull-Up Mid, Stepback Mid, post shots, and other contextual tendencies help determine how those mid-range attempts are created.

Jump Shooting:Shot Mid Right.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from the mid-range area. This acts as the global mid-range volume gate, while Spot-Up Mid, Off-Screen Mid, Dribble Pull-Up Mid, Stepback Mid, post shots, and other contextual tendencies help determine how those mid-range attempts are created.

Jump Shooting:Shot Three Left.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from three-point range. This acts as the global three-point volume gate, while Spot-Up Three, Off-Screen Three, Dribble Pull-Up Three, Stepback Jumper Three, Transition Pull-Up Three, Contested Jumper Three, play types, and team spacing help determine how those attempts are created. This does not determine three-point accuracy.

Jump Shooting:Shot Three Left-Center.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from three-point range. This acts as the global three-point volume gate, while Spot-Up Three, Off-Screen Three, Dribble Pull-Up Three, Stepback Jumper Three, Transition Pull-Up Three, Contested Jumper Three, play types, and team spacing help determine how those attempts are created. This does not determine three-point accuracy.

Jump Shooting:Shot Three Center.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from three-point range. This acts as the global three-point volume gate, while Spot-Up Three, Off-Screen Three, Dribble Pull-Up Three, Stepback Jumper Three, Transition Pull-Up Three, Contested Jumper Three, play types, and team spacing help determine how those attempts are created. This does not determine three-point accuracy.

Jump Shooting:Shot Three Right-Center.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from three-point range. This acts as the global three-point volume gate, while Spot-Up Three, Off-Screen Three, Dribble Pull-Up Three, Stepback Jumper Three, Transition Pull-Up Three, Contested Jumper Three, play types, and team spacing help determine how those attempts are created. This does not determine three-point accuracy.

Jump Shooting:Shot Three Right.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for taking shots from three-point range. This acts as the global three-point volume gate, while Spot-Up Three, Off-Screen Three, Dribble Pull-Up Three, Stepback Jumper Three, Transition Pull-Up Three, Contested Jumper Three, play types, and team spacing help determine how those attempts are created. This does not determine three-point accuracy.

Jump Shooting:Shot Close Left.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for attempting shots from the short close-range area, generally outside the immediate under-basket zone but inside the mid-range area. This can include short push shots, hooks, runners, short fades, and other close attempts. It controls the location preference, while specific tendencies such as Floater or post moves help select the shot type.

Jump Shooting:Shot Close Middle.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for attempting shots from the short close-range area, generally outside the immediate under-basket zone but inside the mid-range area. This can include short push shots, hooks, runners, short fades, and other close attempts. It controls the location preference, while specific tendencies such as Floater or post moves help select the shot type.

Jump Shooting:Shot Close Right.definition: Definition: Overall selection weight for attempting shots from the short close-range area, generally outside the immediate under-basket zone but inside the mid-range area. This can include short push shots, hooks, runners, short fades, and other close attempts. It controls the location preference, while specific tendencies such as Floater or post moves help select the shot type.
